summary.headline: Triton Valves Q1 FY27 group consolidated sales rose 38.5% YoY to ₹186.5 crore; EBITDA ₹12.4 crore, with ₹4.75 crore one-time tax credit lifting PAT to ~₹9.75 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported group consolidated sales of about ₹186.5 crore, up roughly 17.5% QoQ and 38.5% YoY, with about 20% volume growth and the rest value growth. EBITDA was about ₹12.4 crore versus ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY (the slide labelled the YoY figure incorrectly). Gross margin contracted about 145 bps QoQ and 181 bps YoY, which management attributed to commodity pass-through with copper and brass prices near historic highs and the Iran/war disruption. Management also flagged that climate control shrank, metals was hit by delayed Middle East raw material supply, and the merger tax credit flattered PAT.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY
includes ~₹4.75 crore merger tax credit; ~₹5.25 crore excluding it

financial_highlights.value: Down ~145 bps QoQ and ~181 bps YoY
financial_highlights.change: attributed to commodity pass-through, not absolute margin erosion

group capex plan ~₹15 crore for FY27

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Sales ₹103 crore, up from ₹78 crore YoY and ₹86 crore QoQ; growth led by tubeless (~25% volume YoY), TPMS (~75-80% YoY) and EV components (~103% YoY). Tube valves ex-motorcycle segment grew ~20%. Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines running above 85-90% utilisation.

segments.name: Metals (Triton Valves Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹79 crore, up from ~₹50-52 crore YoY and ₹68 crore QoQ; capacity utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, implying ~30% headroom. Current ROCE above 16%, with management targeting 20%+ and possibly 25%. Scrap sales now netted off under Ind AS, reducing reported standalone top line without affecting EBITDA.

segments.name: Climate control
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹3.9 crore, down YoY and QoQ. Management cited Chinese dumping, copper costs and a weak AC season; it is lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected to be quiet, with recovery from Oct-Nov.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a 'reasonably good' Q2 if the second half of the quarter holds, and says FY27 will be much better than FY26.
Annualised Q1 group EBITDA ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26; PBT, EBITDA and revenue expected to run slightly above annualised Q1 levels.
Group ROCE expected to rise from ~12.5% to 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid-next year; new investments targeted at 20-25% internal ROCE.
Ambition of a ₹1,000 crore revenue target by about FY30; management says it has a plan that does not depend on climate control recovery.
EV component vertical targeted at ~₹100 crore over the next few quarters, with climate control also scaling to ~₹100 crore if trade remediation happens.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is not expected until commodity prices stabilise; management said it would take a long time.
Tax credit of ~₹4.75 crore already availed, plus a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore claimed, subject to assessment; no advance tax outflow expected for ~14-15 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 group capex planned at ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore for automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore for metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment).
About 50-60% of the ₹15 crore is expected to be commercialised in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation; management said capacity will run out during the year without investment.
Metals utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, leaving ~30% volume headroom.
Climate control has spare capacity; management said it only needs orders.
demand_pricing: Automotive growth described as ~80% vehicle production growth and ~20% share gain; passenger car and two-wheeler production grew ~12-15% YoY in Q1 (per management).
Management expects automotive growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 but remain positive; new programmes cited with AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch (LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA in TPMS).

Metals: Q1 started slowly from Middle East raw material disruption; ~₹10 crore of metals sales were not delivered on time due to Hormuz issues. Demand strong into Q2; management expects Q3 seasonal traction in metals and climate control.
Prices pass through to automotive and climate control customers every three months. Brass selling price to external customers now above ₹1,000/kg vs ~₹500-550/kg last July-August.
Management expects metals to reach 60%+ of group revenue over 2-3 years; special alloys (naval brass, marine grades) being developed as import substitutes.
Climate control faces Chinese dumping; management is refusing to cut margins to win volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 YoY growth (~38%) came from realisation versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20% was volume growth and the rest value (price/commodity pass-through) growth.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drove volume growth, and how much of metals growth is external versus intercompany for automotive?
qa_highlights.answer: Automotive and metals both grew; management said much of metals sales fed automotive intercompany demand. External sales were about ₹26 crore each for automotive and metals YoY, and ~₹10 crore of metals sales slipped past quarter-end due to Hormuz disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and which segments will it serve?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹15 crore for FY27: ~₹10 crore automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment). About 50-60% to be commercialised in FY27, balance in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is automotive running at maximum utilisation, and can growth sustain into FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are above 85-90% utilisation; tube valves not fully utilised. Volume growth ~18-20% in some segments, 25% tubeless, ~75-80% TPMS, ~103% EV components. Management expects growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 as festive season ends, with new programmes from AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch to offset.

qa_highlights.question: When will double-digit EBITDA margins return, and how do margins look in Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit margin is a long game and depends on commodity stabilisation; it pointed to annualised group EBITDA of ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26 as the absolute-profit measure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the climate control outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was circumspect: Chinese dumping, copper costs and weak AC season hurt the sector; lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected quiet; recovery from Oct-Nov; turnaround needs two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What tax credit is left and what is the cash-tax benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹4.75 crore already availed; a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore subject to assessment. Management said no advance tax outflow for roughly 14-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE targets apply to metals and the group, and what hurdle for new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Metals ROCE is above 16% now, with 20%+ targeted and 25% possible. Group ROCE of ~12.5% expected to reach 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid next year; new investments need 20-25% internal ROCE.

qa_highlights.question: Can the ₹1,000 crore revenue target by FY30 be met without climate control recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a plan B and plan C for the ₹1,000 crore target that does not depend on climate control picking up.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility: copper and brass prices have roughly doubled in a year; percentage gross margin fell 145 bps QoQ and 181 bps YoY, and management gave no timeline for double-digit EBITDA margins.
Capacity constraint: automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines at 85-90%+ utilisation; ~₹10 crore FY27 capex is at risk of delay as only 50-60% is expected to commercialise in FY27.
Metals supply disruption: Middle East/Hormuz raw material shortfall; ~₹10 crore of metals sales not delivered on time in Q1. Q2 performance depends on second-half holding up.
Climate control weakness: sales ~₹3.9 crore; depends on government action (QCO, minimum import price) against Chinese dumping; no recovery expected before Oct-Nov.
Tax credit quality: ~₹4.75 crore one-off merger credit flatters Q1 PAT (~₹9.75 crore vs ~₹5.25 crore ex-credit); further ₹0.3-0.4 crore is subject to assessment.
Working capital and leverage: working capital rose on copper prices; debt to EBITDA ~3x with target of 2.5-3x by year end; cash flow expected to improve over next 2-3 quarters.
Management flagged a seasonal dip in automotive in Q3 after festive season and moderating automotive growth in Q3-Q4; monitor whether volume growth holds at ~20%.
key_quotes: So I'd say about 20 % is volume growth and the rest is, I would say value growth.
I don't want to like forecast too far into the future, but I can only say that we have de risk the business model to a large extent.
I would strongly encourage you to also look at the absolute EBIT, right.
Frankly, internally, we are not very happy with those numbers. But yeah, it was a tough quarter for us.

Usually Q2 is a quiet quarter for the climate control business because AC production kind of goes down during in this rainy season, it picks up again, production picks up from October, November onwards.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and absolute profit growth, but cautious on margins, climate control and FY28 visibility. Management openly declined to forecast beyond Q2 and called Q1 "a tough quarter," while stressing the tax credit and commodity pass-through as explanations.

adds.what: FY27 group capex ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment)

growth.why: Q1 FY27 group sales rose 38.5% YoY to ₹186.5 crore and management guides FY27 revenue above FY26 with a ~₹15 crore capex plan, but automotive lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation, metals has ~30% headroom, climate control is shrinking, and no numeric FY27 revenue growth % is given.
